markdown_report:
At 10% progress, prioritize **learned temporal bias within the corrected HSTU**. Its benefit remains a hypothesis requiring host validation.

**Insights and directions.** Three starting-point insights guide the proposal. (1) Users report stale interests crowding out current needs. This motivates context weighting without assuming every recent interaction matters. (2) Broad associations outrank direct task connections. Temporal context could distinguish ongoing activity from isolated historical interest, but cannot establish equipment compatibility. (3) Industrial has the highest measured training misranking rate, 5.05%. This identifies a separation problem worth testing, without establishing its cause.

Three literature insights constrain implementation. (1) [HSTU](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.17152v3) incorporates relative positional and temporal bias before SiLU aggregation. Adding this mechanism preserves the backbone family. (2) [LIC](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.15817) motivates recovering useful older behavior through temporal context. The [recency study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.09722) cautions against unconditional decay. (3) [Sampling research](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276) finds dataset-dependent tradeoffs. Strong training margins therefore do not justify automatically escalating negative difficulty.

**Framework.** Organize research along three directions: context selection, candidate discrimination, and representation grounding.

| Direction | Existing approach | Proposed experiment | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Context | Position-only HSTU | Learned position-plus-time bias | Current intent remains unobserved |
| Discrimination | Uniform negatives | Moderate lexical curriculum | Unknown false negatives |
| Grounding | Item IDs | Joint title/description encoding | Compatibility remains unverified |

**Candidate assessment.** Scores are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty, each 0–10; higher difficulty means harder. Each cell gives a positive and a limitation.

| Idea | Scores | Critical assessment by axis |
|---|---|---|
| Temporal HSTU | 3/8/8/6/5 | O: faithful extension, established mechanism; P: reusable timing signal, dataset dependent; U: targets stale and weakly supported current interests, cannot verify needs; M: may reduce Industrial errors, temporal cause unmeasured; D: compact bias table, timestamp plumbing required |
| Moderate lexical negatives | 5/6/7/7/4 | O: curriculum combination, familiar sampling; P: sharper discrimination, false negatives; U: challenges broad similarity, may penalize valid alternatives; M: targets separation, training gains may not generalize; D: inference unchanged, filtering requires care |
| Joint text–ID encoding | 4/7/7/5/7 | O: constrained adaptation, existing precedent; P: sparse-item sharing, noisy text; U: exposes specific attributes, cannot certify compatibility; M: may improve representations, no collapse established; D: one network, larger implementation |

**Selected algorithm.** Add a zero-initialized, head-specific temporal bias table to HSTU attention before SiLU. Bucket elapsed times between observed historical events; retain causal masking, positional bias, gating, and normalization. Learn nonmonotonic weights rather than imposing decay.

This explicitly targets stale interests and broad historical associations displacing recent task connections. It also tests whether timing improves Industrial’s measured separation weakness; the supplied diagnostics do not establish temporal causality.

Keep the existing loss initially to isolate the change. Use historical timestamps only, never target-time gaps. Select solely by pinned macro validation HR@10. Preserve four routed checkpoints, predictor consistency, diagnostic interfaces, seeds, and training limits.

idea.description: Extend the corrected HSTU with jointly learned relative temporal bias, retaining one independently trained network and one selected checkpoint per category.
idea.motivation: User feedback identifies stale interests and broad historical associations displacing direct recent connections. Historical timing may help distinguish an ongoing activity from an old isolated interest. Industrial’s 5.05% training negative-beats-positive rate provides a measured model weakness to target, although the supplied results do not establish that missing temporal information causes it.
idea.implementation_notes: Preserve HSTU SiLU attention, gating, positional bias, normalization, and the existing training objective for the first controlled experiment. For each causal historical pair, bucket its nonnegative elapsed time using a documented fixed unit and logarithmic boundaries; represent unavailable timestamps with a separate learned bucket. Initialize additional bias parameters to zero. Never use the next target’s timestamp or future events. Retain log2feats(sequence) through optional historical timestamp arguments or a documented position-only fallback; adapt ModelView and DiagnosisProbe to supply aligned public historical timestamps for temporal probes. Do not infer timestamps from item IDs. Temporal inference requires the authorized history interface to supply or deterministically recover aligned historical event times; otherwise keep this proposal unimplemented rather than silently using inconsistent inputs. Update the predictor writer, checkpoint configuration, timestamp units, bucket definitions, and missing-time behavior together. Read out the greatest nonpadding index for left-padded histories. Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), with measured metrics and definitions. Compare matched timestamp shuffling and recent/old deletion only as in-sample diagnostics, preserving their limitations. Retain all four category routes, DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, at most 200 epochs, and 200 batches per epoch. Use one GPU and select using the fixed host macro validation HR@10. No improvement is claimed before measurement.
idea.pseudocode:
For each category independently:
  initialize corrected HSTU with seed 42
  add zero-initialized per-head temporal-bias embeddings
  for each authorized training batch:
    obtain sequence and aligned historical timestamps
    for causal valid event pairs (i, j):
      bucket[i,j] = log_bucket(max(time[i] - time[j], 0))
      use a dedicated bucket when either timestamp is unavailable
    attention_input = existing_similarity + existing_position_bias + temporal_bias[bucket]
    features = existing_HSTU_SiLU_gated_aggregation(attention_input)
    optimize the unchanged baseline next-item objective
  select one checkpoint using authorized validation
  export the same architecture and temporal preprocessing through the predictor writer
At prediction:
  route to exactly one category checkpoint
  encode only observed history with aligned timestamps
  read features at the greatest nonpadding index
  score candidates through that network's predict_score

originality.positive: A faithful, targeted adaptation of temporal HSTU to the observed stale-interest problem.
originality.negative: Relative temporal bias is already part of published HSTU, so the mechanism itself is established.

future_potential.positive: Provides a compact way to study timing-dependent relevance while allowing older interests to remain useful.
future_potential.negative: Benefits depend on timestamp quality and may be small when positional context already captures the useful signal.

code_difficulty.positive: The architectural addition is a small learned bias table and preserves single-network scoring.
code_difficulty.negative: Aligned timestamp batching, inference plumbing, diagnostic adaptation, and predictor export require careful coordination.

related_work.title: Actions Speak Louder than Words: Trillion-Parameter Sequential Transducers for Generative Recommendations
contributions: Introduces HSTU with gated aggregation and relative positional and temporal attention bias.
Provides direct architectural precedent for the selected extension.
limitations: Does not establish a validation improvement on the four pinned Amazon tasks.
Temporal bias does not inherently impose recency decay or identify purchase intent.

related_work.title: Long-Term Interest Clock
contributions: Motivates using time gaps to recover relevant long-term behaviors.
limitations: Its reported findings do not establish gains for this constrained HSTU experiment.

related_work.title: Study of recency bias in recommendation
contributions: Provides evidence that excessive recency bias can harm recommendation accuracy.
limitations: Does not determine the appropriate temporal weighting for these datasets.

related_work.title: Sequential recommendation negative-sampling study
contributions: Compares sampling strategies and identifies dataset-dependent accuracy and popularity tradeoffs.
limitations: Does not establish that lexical negatives improve the pinned benchmark.
Unobserved items can still be valid alternatives rather than true negatives.

related_work.title: HSTU-BLaIR
contributions: Provides precedent for augmenting HSTU item representations with textual information.
limitations: Its pretrained text encoder is unavailable under the task constraints.
Reported gains do not establish the effectiveness of a text encoder trained from scratch here.
